inspiration.observed_pattern: A grouped parent-child query serializes distinct child JSON_OBJECT values with GROUP_CONCAT, orders the objects by child identifier, and wraps the comma-separated text in JSON array brackets.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a minimized project task export. A repeated task-label row duplicates one child during the join; GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT JSON_OBJECT(...)) removes that multiplication while preserving deterministic task order inside a JSON array-shaped string. The schema, values, aliases, and operational meaning are new.

fixture_notes: Project 701 has two tasks, and the first task is repeated by two labels; DISTINCT must collapse the repeated JSON object while the task IDs retain ascending output order.
determinism_notes: Project ID, task IDs, label IDs, GROUP_CONCAT task ordering, grouping columns, and final project ordering are fixed. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE projects (project_id INT PRIMARY KEY, project_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE project_tasks (task_id INT PRIMARY KEY, project_id INT NOT NULL, task_title VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, task_state VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE task_labels (label_id INT PRIMARY KEY, task_id INT NOT NULL, label_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
INSERT INTO project_tasks VALUES (11, 701, 'Draft brief', 'open'), (12, 701, 'Review copy', 'done')

steps.sql: SELECT p.project_id, p.project_name, CONCAT('[', GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT JSON_OBJECT('task_id', t.task_id, 'title', t.task_title, 'state', t.task_state) ORDER BY t.task_id SEPARATOR ','), ']') AS task_items FROM projects p INNER JOIN project_tasks t ON t.project_id = p.project_id LEFT JOIN task_labels l ON l.task_id = t.task_id GROUP BY p.project_id, p.project_name ORDER BY p.project_id

checks.sql: SELECT p.project_id, t.task_id, l.label_id FROM projects p INNER JOIN project_tasks t ON t.project_id = p.project_id LEFT JOIN task_labels l ON l.task_id = t.task_id ORDER BY p.project_id, t.task_id, l.label_id
